job_description: Applied AI Engineer, San Francisco or remote. Build LLM-powered workflow tools for customer-facing product teams. Work with users, product managers, and engineers to design AI features, evaluate model quality, and ship production APIs. Visa sponsorship and H-1B transfer support available.

Forward Deployed Engineer, Bay Area hybrid. Partner with enterprise customers to understand operational workflows, prototype AI-assisted internal tools, integrate APIs, and translate customer feedback into product improvements. Visa sponsorship not mentioned.

Research Scientist, Machine Learning. Focus on model architecture, pretraining experiments, distributed training, and publishing papers. Strong publication record required. Work location is onsite only. Product or customer-facing work is not part of the role.

AI Platform Infrastructure Engineer. Own Kubernetes clusters, GPU scheduling, service mesh, storage systems, and backend reliability for model serving infrastructure. Minimal product interaction. Visa sponsorship not mentioned.

AI Application Engineer. Build internal LLM tools, write prompts, evaluate output quality, and improve employee productivity workflows. Location, remote policy, and visa sponsorship are not specified.

ML Engineer at a GPU cloud marketplace. Build optimization and orchestration logic that places and tunes ML workloads across a heterogeneous multi-provider fleet. Benchmark GPUs, interconnects, and driver stacks; build tooling, images, and reference stacks; debug performance and reliability across workloads and hardware; turn findings into platform defaults and playbooks; participate in a weekly 24/7 on-call rotation. Requires production ML workloads, GPU memory and throughput knowledge, Linux systems skills, and comfort debugging drivers and networking. Distributed training, large-scale inference, NVIDIA drivers, InfiniBand/RoCE, and cluster networking are preferred. The company is remote-first and offers high ownership, but the JD does not state direct user, customer, domain-expert, or product-workflow collaboration. H-1B transfer support is not mentioned.

NVIDIA's Silicon Co-Design Group is seeking an Applied AI Engineer to develop and integrate AI solutions into the chip design and automation infrastructure used across CPU, GPU, and Tegra SoC production. The engineer will architect and deploy LLM-powered post-silicon validation pipelines, work with cross-functional internal engineering teams to identify workflows where AI can eliminate friction, evaluate emerging AI frameworks and architectures, measure AI impact, and continuously improve the resulting systems. The role requires 5+ years building production ML/AI systems or data-intensive backend services and 2+ years independently owning an AI agent, LLM-powered workflow, or intelligent automation system from prototype through production. It also requires experience in silicon development, chip or system characterization, lab debugging, computer architecture, high-speed interfaces, timing and power fundamentals, and firmware/driver and hardware interaction. Preferred experience includes translating AI research into production tools, launching LLMs, building orchestration agents that manage hundreds to thousands of tools, and using PyTorch or TensorFlow plus NeMo Agent Toolkit, LangChain, Semantic Kernel, AutoGen, CrewAI, or n8n. The posting does not specify Bay Area or remote eligibility, visa sponsorship, or H-1B transfer support.
